readout.summary: Everyone expects Memphis to win; the split is whether it covers 18.5. Memphis (8-3, 5-0 at home) leads the nation in total offense (520.8 yards per game) and is about 91% to win in both ESPN's predictor and the Dimers model. Temple is 2-9 and has lost five straight. Covers, The Rx and Fox's model back Memphis on the spread, while Predictem and Doc's Sports take Temple +17.5 because Memphis allows 209.7 rushing yards a game. Dimers projects 41-22 and, like Covers and Fox, likes the Under. Temple coach K.C. Keeler expects Jaxon Smolik to take most snaps while Ajani Sheppard recovers from an ankle injury. Memphis has allowed 30+ points in four of its last five, so a backdoor cover is the risk.

readout.summary: The consensus is Texas, and the line has moved to -12.5 (ML about -485, total 40.5). Texas (9-2, five straight wins, top 5) can clinch a playoff spot behind a defense Covers and SI Betting rate as the country's best by adjusted EPA per play. Texas A&M (4-7, four straight losses) still hadn't named a starter between Brady Hart and Marcel Reed as of Friday, and its offense ranks 129th in EPA per play. SI Betting and BettorsInsider prefer the Under 40.5, and BettorsInsider also takes A&M +11.5. Texas edge Colin Simmons is questionable (ankle) and Richard Wesley was upgraded to probable; A&M has several players out, including WR Terry Bussey.

readout.summary: Every source read picks Ohio State (7-4) to win at home, but most expect a close, low-scoring game. The line has dropped from 13.5 to about 10-10.5, the total is 37.5-38.5 and the moneyline is about OSU -395 to -430. The case for Ohio State is Jeremiah Smith, the nation's receiving leader, against a Michigan offense ranked 112th in EPA per play and 129th in scoring (18.3 points per game). Ohio State starts freshman Luke Fahey with Julian Sayin out, has lost three of four (including at Nebraska) and is 0-4 against the spread in its last four. The split is on the spread: SI Betting lays the 10, while CBS (six of nine CBS experts on Michigan ATS) and Predictem take Michigan +10.5. Michigan QB Bryce Underwood (hamstring) is questionable but expected to start.

readout.summary: Every source expects LSU (6-5, 3-5 SEC) to win at Arkansas (4-7, 2-6 SEC), but they split on the 14.5-point spread. Tiger Rag's three staff picks have LSU winning by 21-28 and Pick Dawgz lays the points; Yahoo (23-20) and Beatline (24-17) predict a closer LSU win, and Doc's Sports takes Arkansas +12.5. LSU has lost three straight, all as favorites, but each of its six wins came by 21 or more. Arkansas has lost five in a row, most recently 45-3 at Texas; it scores 19.7 points per game (124th) and allows 4.4 yards per carry, worst in the SEC, against an LSU defense allowing 266.5 yards per game. LSU WRs Jackson Harris and Winston Watkins Jr. are questionable again. Yahoo adds that neither team has much to play for, which could keep it close.

readout.summary: No track: Duke is ESPN FPI #25 (power gate). All seven previews pick Wake Forest (10-1, already in the ACC title game) to win, with predicted scores from 27-14 to 38-21. Duke (7-4) has lost two straight and gained only 247 yards in a 20-10 loss to Clemson, when Walker Eget went 16 of 38 for 149 yards. Wake RB Ty Clark III is out for the season. readout.summary: Four of five previews back Tennessee to win and cover -13.5. Their case rests on a defense allowing 14.2 points per game that held LSU to 13 last week, and a run game averaging 213 yards against a Vanderbilt run defense ranked 92nd in opponent EPA per rush. Tennessee is 9-2, playing for a playoff spot and on three straight wins; Vanderbilt is 4-7 (1-7 SEC) after a 34-27 loss at Florida, its fourth loss in five.
